subject: Regional node allocation request — US/EU/APAC deal bundling
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam@helix.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Regional node allocation request — US/EU/APAC deal bundling

Team,

Helix signed an MOU last week for a staged roll-out across three regions (US pilot, EU expansion, APAC pilot). They just shared expected Q3 traffic profiles and an aggressive SLA ask for 99.9% latency under 120ms for user-facing generation endpoints.

Summary of the request (attached: deal-stack-helix.xlsx, initial-sow-helix.pdf):
- US: steady 120 rps peak, big burst windows for model finetune jobs.
- EU: 80 rps peak, strict data locality for EU routing.
- APAC: 40 rps steady with 4x regional burst days.

Ask: I need a recommended dedicated pool sizing and node split per region, with a short fallback plan (burst-to-hosted / cross-region overflow) and a rough cost delta for reserved vs burst capacity. Helix wants a firm number for SOW by EOD Tuesday so their procurement can start PO approvals.

Key constraints to consider:
- Model variants: Llama-3-70B (quantized) for US/EU, smaller 13B variant in APAC during ramp.
- Latency SLOs: user-facing endpoints prioritized; batch finetunes can be queued to Dedicated spare capacity or scheduled nightly.
- Security: EU traffic must stay in EU (they'll request Private/VPC later)

Can you review and propose node counts and an associated rollout plan? I've included the raw traffic matrix in latency-matrix.csv.

Thanks,
Vanessa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: deal-stack-helix.xlsx (spreadsheet), initial-sow-helix.pdf (draft SOW)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Regional node allocation request — US/EU/APAC deal bundling

Vanessa,

Thanks for the context and the attachments — reviewed the traffic CSV. Quick notes from infra perspective:

1) Baseline sizing (sustained) — assuming quantized 70B for user gen and 13B for APAC: 
   - US: 8 dedicated A100-style nodes (continuous) to meet 120 rps with tail latency reserve.
   - EU: 5 dedicated nodes, pinned to EU region for data locality.
   - APAC: 2 dedicated nodes to start, plan for +2 for predictable burst days.

2) Burst strategy — rather than oversized reserves across all regions, recommend:
   - Reserve minimal dedicated capacity per region (above).
   - Enable burst-to-hosted lane for up to 30% of peak in emergency (with cross-region fallback if Helix allows).
   - For APAC burst days, we can provision temporally (on-demand) an extra 2 nodes for up to 72 hours at market pricing.

3) SLO risk and mitigation:
   - If traffic distribution skews higher to long-context generation, token compute could double — add a 20% headroom buffer on US nodes.
   - Canary plan: start US with a canary pool (2 nodes) and ramp to full 8 after 2 weeks post-integration.

4) Cost delta (very rough): reserved vs burst-first approach is ~25% savings on monthly committed spend but increases margin variability if they exceed bursts frequently. We'll need better traffic histograms to refine.

I'll draft a one-pager with the node counts and rollout timeline; can push a version to shared Drive for PO language.

- Karthik
Head of Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Vanessa / Karthik,

Couple of commercial points from my side that will influence how we lock sizing in the SOW:

- Helix wants a committed monthly baseline for the first 12 months with a two-tranche commit: Q3 pilot (lower commit) and Q4 full commit (higher). We should offer a staged committed discount schedule tied to the tranche timing.
- Procurement will ask for clear overage rates and a fallback SLA if they hit burst limits. We should show both: (a) burst pricing to hosted, (b) temporary dedicated add-ons with 72-hour notice.
- If we can include a 2-week canary pilot at a slightly reduced rate (credit), it will ease procurement sign-off.

Proposed commercial packaging to reflect infra plan:
- Pilot tranche (Q3): US 4 nodes reserved / EU 3 nodes / APAC 1 node, with burst allowances.
- Full tranche (Q4): US move to 8 nodes / EU 5 nodes / APAC 3 nodes.

I'll fold this into the SOW language and include the pricing bands. Vanessa — can you confirm Helix's preferred billing currency and whether they require monthly or quarterly invoices? Liam — looping you for confirmation of the billing cadence and any procurement timelines.

—Marissa
Director, Sales Strategy | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

All,

Thanks — aligned on the approach. Final decisions for the SOW:

1) Pilot SOW numbers (to include in the doc shared with Helix):
   - US: 4 reserved nodes + 2-node canary (ramp to 8 in Q4)
   - EU: 3 reserved nodes (EU-only routing) + 2-node burst allowance
   - APAC: 1 reserved node + 2 scheduled on-demand nodes for known burst windows

2) Fallback and SLAs:
   - Burst-to-hosted allowed up to 25% of peak unless Helix explicitly denies cross-region overflow.
   - Overage pricing: explicit per-node-hour rate (include in SOW appendix).

3) Action items and owners:
   - Karthik: produce final node-level technical footprint and expected latency headroom by EOD Wednesday (will attach latency-matrix.csv).
   - Marissa: finalize staged pricing bands and SOW draft (version saved to Drive link).
   - Vanessa: confirm billing cadence with Helix legal/procurement and collect any EU localization requirements.

Liam — please confirm if Helix will accept burst-to-hosted for non-sensitive API calls or if they require strict region-only execution. If they require region-only, we will mark that as a hard constraint and adjust the SOW.

Ben Carter
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
